purpose: Structural validation and evidence-status differences; not a model accuracy benchmark.

luna.finding: No calibrated numerical peer-review score comparison was performed; the pairwise abstract test found preference errors including positive-result bias, but it is not a score-bias estimate.

sol.finding: Selected inferior abstract in 6/10 controlled pairs; failures included positive-result and bombastic-language preference, algorithm-name influence, prompt injection.

luna.finding: No confidence or calibration measure was reported.

sol.finding: Direct unsupported-claim example: title-only RAG input caused critique of a different paper, conflating documents. No quantified false-positive/calibration rate.

luna.finding: No AI–human review agreement or decision agreement was measured.

sol.finding: Evaluator validation α=.93 (95% CI .89,.96) against 253 human-agreed detection labels; human–human α=.73. This validates scoring, not complete-review agreement.

luna.finding: The headline measure is top-k identification accuracy, not conventional recall; the benchmark tests 713 inserted errors but does not report human-comment recall.

sol.finding: Planted-error hit rate @1→@10: GPT 5 9.0%→39.1%; no model exceeds 50%. Top-k success is not precision of all proposed critiques.

luna.finding: No confidence calibration was measured; numerical review scores are outcomes, not self-confidence.

sol.finding: Polarity-reversed critique recognition documents factual-grounding vulnerability, via rating deviation. No direct confidence calibration or adjudicated generated-critique false-positive rate.

luna.finding: A fact-checking module is part of the proposed workflow, but the reported study does not independently score verified scientific-error detection.
No human-comment recall or verified-flaw recall was measured.

sol.finding: Meta(all) five-class macro recall32.4%, F1 28.1%; decision-label recall, not critical-comment/error recall.

luna.finding: The paper analyzes persona tendencies and post-rebuttal sycophancy, but does not report a controlled score-inflation or calibration estimate against paper quality.

sol.finding: Permissive/critical personas skew acceptance/rejection; rebuttal conditioning increases false accept decisions in ablations. Outcome misclassification, not critique false positives.

luna.finding: The evaluation scores atomic strength/weakness points for alignment with human references; it does not adjudicate each point against paper evidence as a verified factual error.

sol.finding: No independently adjudicated scientific-error discovery benchmark; generated-question grounding/constructiveness is judged.

luna.finding: The paper evaluates MAE and alignment but does not establish a directional overrating bias; it notes models can match clustered scores without high review quality.

sol.finding: Prompt-debugging appendix:neutral Qwen/Llama reviews cluster ratings in(8,10); stricter prompts balance scores and can improve MAE without review-quality improvement. No aggregate inflation effect size or denominator supplied.

luna.finding: No confidence calibration or overconfidence outcome was measured.

sol.finding: Question Soundness (joint context support and constructive requested supplement):GPT-5.2 .46,Claude .43 versus human .45, judged by Qwen3-235B. Their “Confidence” criterion means contextual explanation, not self-reported calibration; unsound questions cannot be read as a pure hallucination rate.

luna.finding: Human reference reviews themselves had adjudicated errors: 22.13% of papers and 7.63% of reviews had incorrect opinions identified via inter-reviewer conflict/meta-review adjudication. Model review correctness is separately rated against filtered references.

sol.finding: Correctness is agreement with conflict-filtered review references under an LLM judge; not independently verified manuscript-error discovery.

Direct unsupported visual critiques occur in every tested text-only model, fewer than.05 figure-related opinions/paper; AppendixB.7 shows claims about unseen axes/example diversity. Separate reference-consistency/grounding ratings are not adjudicated false-positive rates; no confidence calibration.

luna.finding: The study measures ratings and error detection, but does not report a distinct model confidence calibration or overconfidence measure.

sol.finding: Direct unsupported-observation finding: text-only reviews describe unprovided figures. Abstract claims “half”, but no audit denominator or detailed result table is supplied; no self-confidence calibration.

luna.finding: Explicit error-aware review produces stricter scores on corrupted papers, but this is an intervention effect and not a calibrated estimate of general score bias.

sol.finding: Explicit error workflow lowers clean ICML overall scores:Gemini8.20→6.81,GPT5 7.27→6.93; corrupted variants also lower. Stricter system scoring is not established human-calibrated accuracy.

luna.finding: No model confidence calibration was measured. The AI-Extra Major Points metric measures divergence from human review coverage; the authors explicitly state extra points are not necessarily incorrect and do not report independent expert validation of AI-only points. Synthetic-error Finding Precision does not establish validity of those additional review critiques.

citations.location: PDF §5.2; Appendix B.4, Coverage-based Alignment Protocol

sol.finding: Qualitative over-criticality:deeper modes sometimes elevate borderline or debatable issues; unmatched findings are explicitly not necessarily false positives. No adjudicated aggregate invalid-critique rate or direct confidence calibration.

note: Same status does not establish the same finding or numerical accuracy. Differences may reflect source versions, scope, or interpretation; review citations.
